focus.jtag: U.S. and Iran paused hostilities over the weekend — oil tumbles, futures rallied at the open, VIX eases — but a chip selloff is dragging tech, and FOMC + four mega-caps + PCE all land this week
focus.jnote: The environment eased over the weekend — but the calendar is a minefield. The U.S. suspended its airstrike campaign against Iran late Friday to allow diplomacy, and Tehran said it would hold fire under an “attack for attack” framework as long as the U.S. pause holds. The relief flowed straight into markets: oil dropped 5–7% (WTI ~$84, Brent ~$90) as the Hormuz risk premium came out, equity futures opened up (S&P ~+0.8%, Nasdaq ~+1.3%), gold ticked up toward $4,090, and the VIX slipped toward ~17.6. That is the good news. The bad news is twofold: a broad semiconductor selloff (SMH ~−3.7%, ASML ~−8%, AMD/Teradyne ~−7%, Micron ~−6%) is dragging the Nasdaq back into the red intraday, and the schedule is the busiest week of the quarter — the FOMC decision Wed 7/29 (hold expected, ~30% hike bet live), Microsoft and Meta Wed, Apple and Amazon Thu, and June Core PCE Fri. This is a wait-for-it tape, not a sell-premium-into-it tape.
focus.notdown: Mega-cap tech (MSFT, META, AAPL, AMZN) caught an early relief bid as oil fell and rate-hike fear eased, but chips are rolling over hard intraday. Be honest: all four report this week — MSFT/META Wed, AAPL/AMZN Thu — so earnings risk sits inside any normal DTE. The bid is real but pre-earnings; a bull put here is a coin-flip on a binary print. Watch-only.
focus.notup: Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX) is a clear laggard as crude gives back the war premium — the fundamental lean is down. But XOM & CVX report this week too, and selling a bear call the morning after a 5–7% oil drop invites a snap-back on any Iran headline reversal. With no verified scanner, the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why YELLOW (not GREEN)? Two hard locks. First, the calendar: FOMC Wed 7/29 plus Core PCE Fri are exactly the scheduled events the master prompt says cannot carry a GREEN verdict — and MSFT/META/AAPL/AMZN stack single-stock gap risk on top. Second: no verified scanner data is available today, so the setups below are hand-built from news, not machine-screened. Composite 48 and P(≥1% gap) 33% are benign, but with a Fed-plus-mega-cap gauntlet ahead and a chip rout underway, there is little to do. Stand aside on new spreads; keep any existing position clear of every print and the Fed. Cash is a position this week.

risks: FOMC decision · Wed 7/29 — a hold is widely expected, but markets price a live ~30% hike bet and ~80% odds of a September move. The press conference is the swing factor. This is the week's number-one scheduled event.

MSFT & META Wed · AAPL & AMZN Thu — four of the most valuable companies report within 48 hours, and roughly a third of the S&P reports this week. After the hyperscaler AI-capex scare, the bar on spending is high; any one gap can move the whole index. Keep every spread clear of these prints.

June Core PCE · Fri — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge lands the same week as the decision, alongside advance Q2 GDP. A hot print stacked on the recent oil spike would revive the rate-hike narrative and pressure stocks.

Iran pause reversal — the de-escalation driving today's oil drop and relief rally is unofficial and fragile; Tehran only holds fire “as long as the U.S. pause holds.” Any breakdown re-spikes crude through Hormuz and gaps the whole tape back down.

Chip rout & the 10-year — SMH ~−3.7% with ASML ~−8% and AMD/MU sharply lower on AI-capex fear, while the 10Y sits ~4.64% off its ~4.71% high. A tech-led slide or a rate pop back toward 4.7% compounds pressure on equities.

earnings.intro: This is the busiest earnings week of the quarter, stacked on top of the FOMC decision — roughly a third of the S&P 500 reports. Microsoft and Meta report Wed 7/29; Apple and Amazon Thu 7/30; energy majors XOM & CVX and consumer/industrial names (PG, KO, BA, F) are scattered through the week — all alongside the Fed (Wed) and June Core PCE (Fri). A single-stock earnings gap on top of a policy decision is a double catalyst — keep every spread clear of its name's print and out to a DTE that clears the Fed.
